fixes.explanation: City gates make sense, friend. That's where people did their business and their arguing. But Hosea 9:8 says, "Hostility is in the house of his God!" I think that's the part that makes you read it twice, because the house of God is the last place you'd look for it.

Shiloh, friend? I get it, it's a big Bible name and it just feels right. But Hosea 9:15 says, "All their evil appears at Gilgal, for there I hated them." The LORD names Gilgal, so Gilgal is the place. I think it's a heavy line, and we can let it sit.

A broken treaty is a sharp guess, friend, since kings get into trouble that way all the time. But Hosea 9:17 says, "My God will reject them because they have not obeyed Him…" The verse gives no treaty at all. The reason is simply that they did not obey Him, and that's the one to hold onto.
